records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֵּ֥רֶד יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת אֶחָ֑יו וַיֵּ֛ט עַד־אִ֥ישׁ עֲדֻלָּמִ֖י וּשְׁמ֥וֹ חִירָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was at that time, and went down Judah from with his brothers and turned aside to a man, an Adullamite, and his name [was] Hirah.
pieces: It was at about this time that Judah parted company with his brothers. He went down and pitched his tent near Hirah, a man from the town of Adullam.

L.1: And it happened at that time that Judah went down from his brothers and turned aside to a certain Adullamite whose name [was] Hirah.

R.1: Around that time Judah went away from his brothers. He went down and made his home near Hirah, a man from the town of Adullam.

decisions.choice: at that time: a loose link to the sale of Joseph
alternatives: at exactly the time Joseph was sold
decisions.reason: The story of Joseph pauses here and picks up again in 39:1. The events of this chapter cover many years (Judah's sons grow up and marry), so "at that time" sets them in the same period of the family's life rather than the same week. Placed here, Judah's story stands beside Joseph's: the brother who proposed selling Joseph (37:26-27) leaves the family and is later changed.

decisions.choice: went down ... turned aside to: moved to the lowlands and settled near Hirah
decisions.reason: Adullam lay in the low hills west of the hill country around Hebron, so Judah "went down". To "turn aside to" someone is to stop and lodge with or near him; Hirah stays Judah's friend through the chapter (verses 12, 20).

decisions.choice: a man from the town of Adullam
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the name of his people as the name of his town.

records.source: וַיַּרְא־שָׁ֧ם יְהוּדָ֛ה בַּת־אִ֥ישׁ כְּנַעֲנִ֖י וּשְׁמ֣וֹ שׁ֑וּעַ וַיִּקָּחֶ֖הָ וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And saw there Judah a daughter of a man, a Canaanite, and his name [was] Shua; and he took her and went in to her.
pieces: There Judah caught sight of a woman, the daughter of a Canaanite called Shua. He took her as his wife and lay with her.

L.2: And Judah saw there the daughter of a Canaanite man whose name [was] Shua, and he took her and went in to her.

R.2: In that place Judah noticed the daughter of a Canaanite man called Shua. Judah married her, and they lived together as husband and wife.

decisions.choice: a Canaanite: Judah marries outside the family line
decisions.reason: Abraham and Isaac took care that their sons should not marry Canaanite women (24:3; 28:1). Judah does so without comment from the narrator; the mixing with Canaanite ways is part of the background of this chapter.

decisions.choice: his name was Shua: the name is her father's
decisions.reason: "His name" refers to the man, her father. The woman herself is never named; she is called "the daughter of Shua" (verse 12; in 1 Chronicles 2:3, Bath-shua).

decisions.choice: took her and went in to her: married her and slept with her
decisions.reason: "Took" is the usual word for taking a wife, and "went in to" is the usual way of describing sexual union.

decisions.choice: they lived together as husband and wife
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom in plain, modest words.

records.source: וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ עֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
pieces: She conceived and bore a son, and Judah called him Er.

L.3: And she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.

R.3: She became pregnant, and her first child was a boy. Judah called him Er.

decisions.choice: he called (the Hebrew text) or she called
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text says the father named the first son. The Samaritan Pentateuch and some Hebrew manuscripts read "she called", as in verses 4 and 5, where the mother names the next two sons. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Judah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Judah as the one who named the boy.

records.source: וַתַּ֥הַר ע֖וֹד וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ אוֹנָֽן׃
records.gloss: And she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
pieces: She conceived again and bore another son, whom she called Onan.

L.4: And she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.

R.4: Later she had a second son. She called him Onan.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤סֶף עוֹד֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵׁלָ֑ה וְהָיָ֥ה בִכְזִ֖יב בְּלִדְתָּ֥הּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And she again bore a son and called his name Shelah; and he was in Kezib when she bore him.
pieces: Then she had yet another son, and she named him Shelah. Judah was at Kezib when she gave birth to him.

L.5: And yet again she bore a son and called his name Shelah. And he was at Kezib when she bore him.

R.5: Her third son she named Shelah. Judah was at the town of Kezib when the boy was born.

decisions.choice: he was at Kezib: Judah was at Kezib
alternatives: the child was born at Kezib
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he was", most naturally Judah, so that Shelah was born while Judah was at Kezib. The ancient Greek translation reads "she was". Kezib is probably the town called Achzib near Adullam (Joshua 15:44). Its name sounds like a word for "deceive" or "fail" (Micah 1:14 plays on it), perhaps a hint of Judah's failure to give Shelah to Tamar.

decisions.choice: Judah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Judah, the most likely subject.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֧ח יְהוּדָ֛ה אִשָּׁ֖ה לְעֵ֣ר בְּכוֹר֑וֹ וּשְׁמָ֖הּ תָּמָֽר׃
records.gloss: And took Judah a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name [was] Tamar.
pieces: For Er, his firstborn, Judah found a wife whose name was Tamar.

L.6: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name [was] Tamar.

R.6: Judah found a wife for his oldest son Er. She was called Tamar.

decisions.choice: Judah took a wife for Er: the father arranged the marriage
decisions.reason: Marriages were arranged by the head of the family (24:4; 28:2). Judah's choice binds Tamar to his household, which is why he still has authority over her in verses 11 and 24.

decisions.choice: Tamar: "date palm"
decisions.reason: The name means a date palm, a tall and fruitful tree. Her nationality is not given.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י עֵ֚ר בְּכ֣וֹר יְהוּדָ֔ה רַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְמִתֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was Er, the firstborn of Judah, evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and put him to death Yahweh.
pieces: But Judah's firstborn, Er, was evil in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s eyes, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought his life to an end.

L.7: But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put him to death.

R.7: Er did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw as evil, so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} caused him to die.

decisions.choice: Er ... evil: a play on letters
decisions.reason: The letters of Er's name ('er) reversed give the word for "evil" (ra'). The narrator names no particular sin; the point is that the firstborn is set aside.

decisions.choice: the LORD put him to death: God judges within Judah's family
decisions.reason: This is the first time Genesis says that the LORD put a particular person to death. Judah does not see the hand of God in it; he blames Tamar (verse 11).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוּדָה֙ לְאוֹנָ֔ן בֹּ֛א אֶל־אֵ֥שֶׁת אָחִ֖יךָ וְיַבֵּ֣ם אֹתָ֑הּ וְהָקֵ֥ם זֶ֖רַע לְאָחִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Judah to Onan, go in to the wife of your brother and perform the duty of a husband's brother for her and raise up offspring for your brother.
pieces: Judah told Onan, "Go to your brother's widow and carry out the brother-in-law's duty: marry her and so give your brother descendants."

L.8: And Judah said to Onan, "Go in to your brother's wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother."

R.8: Then Judah told Onan, "Your brother died without children. You must marry his widow. Then the children you have with her will count as your brother's descendants."

decisions.choice: perform the duty of a brother-in-law: the custom later called levirate marriage
decisions.reason: When a man died without a son, his brother was to marry the widow, and the first son born to them counted as the dead man's son, carrying his name and inheriting his share (Deuteronomy 25:5-10; Ruth 4:5, 10). The custom protected the widow and kept the dead man's line alive.

decisions.choice: raise up offspring for your brother: give him an heir
decisions.reason: The child would legally be Er's, not Onan's (verse 9).

decisions.choice: Your brother died without children ... will count as your brother's descendants
alternatives: Go in to your brother's wife and perform the duty
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the custom that Judah's words assume.

records.source: וַיֵּ֣דַע אוֹנָ֔ן כִּ֛י לֹּ֥אל֖וֹ יִהְיֶ֣ה הַזָּ֑רַע וְהָיָ֞ה אִם־בָּ֨א אֶל־אֵ֤שֶׁת אָחִיו֙ וְשִׁחֵ֣ת אַ֔רְצָה לְבִלְתִּ֥י נְתָן־זֶ֖רַע לְאָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And knew Onan that not to him would be the offspring; and it was, whenever he went in to the wife of his brother, he spoiled [it] to the ground so as not to give offspring to his brother.
pieces: Onan, however, knew that any children would not be counted as his. So each time he lay with his brother's widow, he made sure his seed was wasted on the ground, to avoid giving his brother descendants.

L.9: But Onan knew that the offspring would not be his; so whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he wasted [his seed] on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.

R.9: Onan was aware that any child born would be counted as his brother's, not his own. So when he lay with Tamar, he always made sure she could not become pregnant. He refused to give his brother descendants.

decisions.choice: whenever he went in: a repeated practice
decisions.reason: The form describes what Onan did each time. He took the widow as his wife but refused the purpose for which he married her.

decisions.choice: spoiled it to the ground: let his seed fall on the ground
decisions.reason: The phrase describes withdrawal so that she would not conceive. The wrong lies in refusing his duty to his dead brother and to Tamar while appearing to fulfill it.

decisions.choice: the offspring would not be his: an heir would cut his inheritance
decisions.reason: As the firstborn's son, Er's heir would receive the firstborn's share. Without one, more of Judah's estate would come to Onan. The text does not state this motive, but the custom implies it.

decisions.choice: he always made sure she could not become pregnant
alternatives: he wasted his seed on the ground
decisions.reason: Readable states the result in plain words.

records.source: וַיֵּ֛רַע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיָּ֖מֶת גַּם־אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And was evil in the eyes of Yahweh what he did, and he put to death also him.
pieces: Onan's deed was evil in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s eyes, and Onan too died by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hand.

L.10: And what he did was evil in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put him to death also.

R.10: In {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s eyes Onan's act was evil. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} ended Onan's life as well.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָה֩ לְתָמָ֨ר כַּלָּת֜וֹ שְׁבִ֧י אַלְמָנָ֣ה בֵית־אָבִ֗יךְ עַד־יִגְדַּל֙ שֵׁלָ֣ה בְנִ֔י כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר פֶּן־יָמ֥וּת גַּם־ה֖וּא כְּאֶחָ֑יו וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ תָּמָ֔ר וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And said Judah to Tamar his daughter-in-law, remain a widow [in] the house of your father until grows up Shelah my son; for he said, lest die also he like his brothers. And went Tamar and dwelt [in] the house of her father.
pieces: Judah then said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Go on as a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah is grown." For he was thinking, "Otherwise he too may die, as his brothers did." So Tamar went and made her home in her father's house.

L.11: And Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Remain a widow [in] your father's house until Shelah my son grows up"; for he said, "Lest he also die like his brothers." And Tamar went and lived [in] her father's house.

R.11: Judah told Tamar, "Return to your father's house. Live there as a widow until my son Shelah is a man." Judah said this because he feared that Shelah might die as his brothers did. So Tamar went and lived with her father.

decisions.choice: for he said: he said to himself, he thought
decisions.reason: "Said" here means what Judah thought but did not tell Tamar. The narrator lets the reader see that Judah's promise was not meant to be kept (verse 14).

decisions.choice: remain a widow in your father's house: still bound to Judah's family
decisions.reason: Tamar returns to her father's house but remains promised to Shelah. She is not free to marry anyone else, which is why her pregnancy is treated as unfaithfulness in verse 24.

decisions.choice: Judah said this because he feared
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that this was Judah's private thought, not what he told Tamar.

records.source: וַיִּרְבּוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַתָּ֖מָת בַּת־שׁ֣וּעַ אֵֽשֶׁת־יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּ֜עַל עַל־גֹּֽזֲזֵ֤י צֹאנוֹ֙ ה֗וּא וְחִירָ֛ה רֵעֵ֥הוּ הָעֲדֻלָּמִ֖י תִּמְנָֽתָה׃
records.gloss: And increased the days, and died the daughter of Shua, the wife of Judah; and was comforted Judah and went up to the shearers of his sheep, he and Hirah his friend the Adullamite, to Timnah.
pieces: Years went by, and Shua's daughter, Judah's wife, died. After he had been consoled, Judah went up to Timnah with his friend Hirah from Adullam, to be with the men shearing his flocks.

L.12: And the days became many, and the daughter of Shua, Judah's wife, died. And Judah was comforted, and he went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.

R.12: Years later Judah's wife died. After Judah had grieved for her and been comforted, he went up to the town of Timnah, where workers were cutting the wool from his sheep. Hirah, his friend from Adullam, went along.

decisions.choice: Judah was comforted: his time of mourning ended
decisions.reason: To be comforted is to come to the end of mourning. Judah, now a widower, is free to go out to the shearing.

decisions.choice: the sheepshearers: a time of feasting
decisions.reason: Shearing was a festive season with eating and drinking (1 Samuel 25:2-8; 2 Samuel 13:23-28). Timnah lay in the hill country (Joshua 15:57), so Judah "went up".

decisions.choice: Years went by
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom: a long time passed.

records.source: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְתָמָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֥ה חָמִ֛יךְ עֹלֶ֥ה תִמְנָ֖תָה לָגֹ֥ז צֹאנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was told to Tamar, saying, behold, your father-in-law [is] going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.
pieces: Word reached Tamar: "Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah for the shearing of his sheep."

L.13: And it was told to Tamar, saying, "Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep."

R.13: Tamar was given this news: "Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah. It is time to shear his sheep."

records.source: וַתָּסַר֩ בִּגְדֵ֨י אַלְמְנוּתָ֜הּ מֵֽעָלֶ֗יהָ וַתְּכַ֤ס בַּצָּעִיף֙ וַתִּתְעַלָּ֔ף וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח עֵינַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־דֶּ֣רֶךְ תִּמְנָ֑תָה כִּ֤י רָאֲתָה֙ כִּֽי־גָדַ֣ל שֵׁלָ֔ה וְהִ֕וא לֹֽא־נִתְּנָ֥ה ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And she removed the garments of her widowhood from on her and covered herself with the veil and wrapped herself, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which [is] on the road to Timnah; for she saw that had grown up Shelah, and she had not been given to him as a wife.
pieces: So she laid aside her widow's clothing, put on a veil and wrapped herself up, and took a seat at the gateway of Enaim, which lies on the road to Timnah. She could see that Shelah was now grown, and still she had not been given to him as his wife.

L.14: And she took off her widow's garments and covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself up, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which [is] on the road to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she had not been given to him as a wife.

R.14: So Tamar changed out of the clothes she wore as a widow. She put on a veil and wrapped herself up so that she would not be recognized. Then she went and sat at the gate of Enaim, a town on the way to Timnah. She did this because Shelah was now grown, yet Judah had not given her to him as his wife.

decisions.choice: the garments of her widowhood: clothing that showed she was a widow
decisions.reason: A widow wore clothing that marked her state. By taking it off and veiling herself, Tamar hides who she is.

decisions.choice: the entrance of Enaim: a town gate or a fork in the road
alternatives: at the opening of the eyes
decisions.reason: Enaim ("two springs" or "two eyes") is probably the town called Enam in Joshua 15:34. The phrase can also be read "at the opening of the eyes", which fits the story: Tamar sits where Judah's eyes will at last be opened.

decisions.choice: for she saw: the reason for her plan
decisions.reason: The narrator gives Tamar's motive: Judah has broken his word. She acts to obtain the child that the custom owed her dead husband.

decisions.choice: so that she would not be recognized
decisions.reason: Readable states the purpose of the veil, which verses 15-16 make plain.

records.source: וַיִּרְאֶ֣הָ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַֽיַּחְשְׁבֶ֖הָ לְזוֹנָ֑ה כִּ֥י כִסְּתָ֖ה פָּנֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And saw her Judah and considered her to be a prostitute, for she had covered her face.
pieces: Judah saw her and took her for a prostitute, since her face was veiled.

L.15: And Judah saw her and took her to be a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

R.15: Judah saw her, but he could not see her face because of the veil. So he thought she was a prostitute.

decisions.choice: for she had covered her face: why he did not know her
decisions.reason: The veil explains why Judah did not recognize her. Whether it also marked her as a prostitute is not clear; brides were veiled too (24:65), and nothing else in Scripture says prostitutes wore veils. Her sitting by the road may have been what suggested it.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨ט אֵלֶ֜יהָ אֶל־הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽבָה־נָּא֙ אָב֣וֹא אֵלַ֔יִךְ כִּ֚י לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י כַלָּת֖וֹ הִ֑וא וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מַה־תִּתֶּן־לִּ֔יכִּ֥י תָב֖וֹא אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he turned aside to her to the road and said, give, please, let me go in to you — for not he knew that his daughter-in-law she [was] — and she said, what will you give to me that you may come in to me?
pieces: He turned off the road toward her. "Come," he said, "let me lie with you." He did not know she was his daughter-in-law. "And what will you give me for it?" she answered.

L.16: And he turned aside to her by the road and said, "Come now, let me come in to you"; for he did not know that she [was] his daughter-in-law. And she said, "What will you give me, that you may come in to me?"

R.16: He left the road and walked over to her. "Come here," he said. "I want to go to bed with you." He had no idea she was his daughter-in-law. She asked, "What will you pay me for it?"

decisions.choice: he did not know: the narrator clears Judah of knowing incest
decisions.reason: The aside makes clear that Judah did not knowingly lie with his daughter-in-law, an act later forbidden (Leviticus 18:15). His fault is visiting a prostitute and breaking his word.

decisions.choice: what will you give me?: Tamar sets a price
decisions.reason: She bargains as a prostitute would, but her aim is the pledge that will prove who the father is (verse 18).

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֛י אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח גְּדִֽי־עִזִּ֖ים מִן־הַצֹּ֑אן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר אִם־תִּתֵּ֥ן עֵרָב֖וֹן עַ֥ד שָׁלְחֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And he said, I, I will send a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said, if you will give a pledge until you send [it].
pieces: "I will have a young goat sent to you from the flock," he said. She answered, "Yes, if you hand me something to keep as a guarantee until you send it."

L.17: And he said, "I will send a young goat from the flock." And she said, "[Only] if you give a pledge until you send [it]."

R.17: Judah promised, "I will have a young goat brought to you from my flock." "Then leave something with me until it comes," she said.

decisions.choice: a young goat: the same animal as in Jacob's deceptions
decisions.reason: Judah and his brothers deceived their father with a goat's blood on Joseph's robe (37:31), as Jacob had deceived Isaac with young goats and his brother's clothes (27:9, 16). Now Judah is the one deceived, and a young goat is the price.

decisions.choice: a pledge: security held until payment
decisions.reason: An 'eravon is something given as a guarantee and returned when the debt is paid.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מָ֣ה הָֽעֵרָבוֹן֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶתֶּן־לָּךְ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר חֹתָֽמְךָ֙ וּפְתִילֶ֔ךָ וּמַטְּךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיִּתֶּן־לָּ֛הּ וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ וַתַּ֥הַר לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he said, what [is] the pledge which I shall give to you? And she said, your seal and your cord and your staff which [is] in your hand. And he gave [them] to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
pieces: "What do you want as security?" he asked. "Your seal on its cord," she said, "and the staff in your hand." So he handed them over and lay with her, and she conceived a child by him.

L.18: And he said, "What [is] the pledge that I should give you?" And she said, "Your seal and your cord and your staff that [is] in your hand." And he gave [them] to her and came in to her, and she conceived by him.

R.18: "What do you want me to leave with you?" he asked. "The seal you wear on a cord," she said, "and that walking stick in your hand." Judah handed them over. He slept with her, and she became pregnant with his child.

decisions.choice: seal, cord and staff: the marks of a man's identity
decisions.reason: A seal was a small engraved stone, often a cylinder worn on a cord around the neck, pressed into clay to sign agreements. A leader's staff was also personal and recognizable. Together they identified Judah beyond doubt, a far greater pledge than a goat was worth.

decisions.choice: walking stick
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for the staff.

records.source: וַתָּ֣קָם וַתֵּ֔לֶךְ וַתָּ֥סַר צְעִיפָ֖הּ מֵעָלֶ֑יהָ וַתִּלְבַּ֖שׁ בִּגְדֵ֥י אַלְמְנוּתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And she arose and went and removed her veil from on her and put on the garments of her widowhood.
pieces: Then she rose and went away. She laid aside her veil and put her widow's clothing back on.

L.19: And she arose and went away, and removed her veil from her and put on her widow's garments.

R.19: Tamar got up and went away. She removed the veil and dressed once more as a widow.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְהוּדָ֜ה אֶת־גְּדִ֣י הָֽעִזִּ֗ים בְּיַד֙ רֵעֵ֣הוּ הָֽעֲדֻלָּמִ֔י לָקַ֥חַת הָעֵרָב֖וֹן מִיַּ֣ד הָאִשָּׁ֑ה וְלֹ֖א מְצָאָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And sent Judah the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite to take the pledge from the hand of the woman, and he did not find her.
pieces: Judah had his friend the Adullamite take the young goat, so as to get back the pledge from the woman, but the friend found no trace of her.

L.20: And Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend the Adullamite to take back the pledge from the woman's hand, but he did not find her.

R.20: Judah gave the young goat to his friend Hirah to deliver. Hirah was to bring back Judah's seal and walking stick. But the woman was nowhere to be found.

decisions.choice: Hirah ... Judah's seal and walking stick
decisions.reason: Readable names the friend and the items of the pledge.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֤י מְקֹמָהּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַיֵּ֧ה הַקְּדֵשָׁ֛ה הִ֥וא בָעֵינַ֖יִם עַל־הַדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה בָזֶ֖ה קְדֵשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And he asked the men of her place, saying, where [is] the consecrated woman, she [who was] at Enaim by the road? And they said, there has not been in this [place] a consecrated woman.
pieces: He inquired of the local men, "The shrine prostitute who sat by the roadside at Enaim, where is she?" They replied, "We have had no shrine prostitute here."

L.21: And he asked the men of her place, saying, "Where [is] the consecrated woman who [was] at Enaim by the road?" And they said, "There has been no consecrated woman here."

R.21: Hirah asked the men who lived there about the shrine prostitute who had been by the road at Enaim. "Where is she?" he said. But they answered, "No woman like that has ever been here."

decisions.choice: the qedeshah: a woman connected with a shrine
decisions.reason: Qedeshah comes from the word for "holy" or "set apart". In Deuteronomy 23:17-18 and Hosea 4:14 it stands beside the word for a prostitute, so it refers to a woman whose prostitution was linked with a shrine. How such women served is uncertain. Hirah uses this more respectable word where the narrator and Judah use the ordinary word (verses 15, 24).

decisions.choice: the men of her place (the Hebrew text) or the men of the place
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "her place". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the ancient Greek translation read "the place", as in verse 22. The meaning is the same: the people who lived there.

decisions.choice: consecrated woman
decisions.reason: Literal shows the root meaning of the word; Balanced and Readable give its sense in this setting.

records.source: וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ אֶל־יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹ֣א מְצָאתִ֑יהָ וְגַ֨ם אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה בָזֶ֖ה קְדֵשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And he returned to Judah and said, not I found her; and also the men of the place said, there has not been in this [place] a consecrated woman.
pieces: He came back to Judah and reported, "I did not find her. What is more, the local men said, 'We have had no shrine prostitute here.'"

L.22: And he returned to Judah and said, "I did not find her; and also the men of the place said, 'There has been no consecrated woman here.'"

R.22: Hirah returned to Judah. "She was not there," he said. "The men of the place even told me that there had never been a shrine prostitute there."

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוּדָה֙ תִּֽקַּֽח־לָ֔הּ פֶּ֖ן נִהְיֶ֣ה לָב֑וּז הִנֵּ֤ה שָׁלַ֨חְתִּי֙ הַגְּדִ֣י הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹ֥א מְצָאתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And said Judah, let her take [them] for herself, lest we become a contempt; behold, I sent this kid, and you, not you found her.
pieces: "Let her have the things, then," said Judah. "We do not want people laughing at us. As you know, I sent this young goat, and you could not find her."

L.23: And Judah said, "Let her keep [them] for herself, lest we become a laughingstock. Look, I sent this young goat, and you did not find her."

R.23: Judah said, "Let her keep them. If we keep looking, people will laugh at us. I tried to pay her with this goat, but you could not find her."

decisions.choice: lest we become a laughingstock: Judah protects his name
decisions.reason: To go on asking for a prostitute would make Judah a joke. He would rather lose his seal and staff than his reputation. The irony is that the pledge he gives up will soon expose him.

decisions.choice: If we keep looking
decisions.reason: Readable states what would make them a laughingstock.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀כְּמִשְׁלֹ֣שׁחֳדָשִׁ֗ים וַיֻּגַּ֨ד לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה לֵֽאמֹר֙ זָֽנְתָה֙ תָּמָ֣ר כַּלָּתֶ֔ךָ וְגַ֛ם הִנֵּ֥ה הָרָ֖ה לִזְנוּנִ֑ים וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֔ה הוֹצִיא֖וּהָ וְתִשָּׂרֵֽף׃
records.gloss: And it was about three months [later], and it was told to Judah, saying, has played the prostitute Tamar your daughter-in-law, and also behold, she [is] pregnant by prostitution. And said Judah, bring her out, and let her be burned.
pieces: Some three months went by. Then word came to Judah: "Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has prostituted herself, and she is even pregnant from it." "Take her out," Judah ordered, "and let her be burned."

L.24: And it happened about three months [later] that it was told to Judah, saying, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the prostitute, and moreover, look, she [is] pregnant by prostitution." And Judah said, "Bring her out, and let her be burned."

R.24: Three months or so passed. Then people came to Judah and said, "Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has behaved like a prostitute, and because of that she is pregnant." Judah ordered, "Bring her out here. She must be burned to death."

decisions.choice: played the prostitute: been sexually unfaithful
decisions.reason: The verb (zanah) covers prostitution and any sexual unfaithfulness. Since Tamar was promised to Shelah, her pregnancy was treated as unfaithfulness to Judah's family.

decisions.choice: let her be burned: Judah acts as judge of his household
decisions.reason: As head of the family to which Tamar was bound, Judah passes sentence. Burning is later the penalty for a priest's daughter who becomes a prostitute (Leviticus 21:9). Judah condemns her for the very thing he has done himself.

records.source: הִ֣וא מוּצֵ֗את וְהִ֨יא שָׁלְחָ֤ה אֶל־חָמִ֨יהָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֣לֶּה לּ֔וֹ אָנֹכִ֖י הָרָ֑ה וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַכֶּר־נָ֔א לְמִ֞י הַחֹתֶ֧מֶת וְהַפְּתִילִ֛ים וְהַמַּטֶּ֖ה הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: She [was] being brought out, and she sent to her father-in-law, saying, by a man to whom these [belong] I [am] pregnant. And she said, examine, please: to whom [belong] the seal and the cords and the staff, these?
pieces: Even as she was being led out, she sent this word to her father-in-law: "The man these things belong to is the one who made me pregnant." She added, "Please examine them. Whose are they, this seal and cord and staff?"

L.25: As she was being brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, "By the man to whom these [belong] I [am] pregnant." And she said, "Please examine [them]: whose [are] these, the seal and the cords and the staff?"

R.25: While she was being led out, Tamar sent word to Judah: "These things belong to the man who got me pregnant. Look at them closely. Whose seal, cord and walking stick are they?"

decisions.choice: examine, please (hakker-na): the words Judah's brothers once used
decisions.reason: The same words were used when Joseph's bloodied robe was brought to Jacob (37:32). Judah, who helped deceive his father with "examine, please", now hears them himself.

decisions.choice: she sent to her father-in-law: she does not accuse him openly
decisions.reason: Tamar sends the pledge privately rather than naming Judah in public. She leaves it to him to recognize the items and to confess.

decisions.choice: Judah
decisions.reason: Readable names him.

records.source: וַיַּכֵּ֣ר יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ צָֽדְקָ֣ה מִמֶּ֔נִּי כִּֽי־עַל־כֵּ֥ן לֹא־נְתַתִּ֖יהָ לְשֵׁלָ֣ה בְנִ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָסַ֥ף ע֖וֹד לְדַעְתָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And recognized Judah and said, she is righteous more than I, for therefore not I gave her to Shelah my son. And not he again any more to know her.
pieces: Judah saw that they were his. "She has been more righteous than I have," he said, "because I would not let her marry my son Shelah." He never had relations with her again.

L.26: And Judah recognized [them] and said, "She is more righteous than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son." And he did not know her again.

R.26: Judah knew the things were his. "She is more righteous than I am," he said, "because I kept my son Shelah from her." Judah did not sleep with her after that.

decisions.choice: she is more righteous than I: she is in the right, not I
alternatives: she is right and I am wrong
decisions.reason: The phrase can compare the two (she is more in the right) or simply declare her in the right over against him. Either way Judah admits that Tamar acted to keep the family duty he had refused. "Righteous" here means doing what a relationship requires.

decisions.choice: Judah recognized: the turning point in Judah's life
decisions.reason: Judah owns his wrong publicly. The man who once sold his brother will later offer himself as a slave in place of Benjamin (44:18-34).

decisions.choice: know her: have sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: "Know" is used for sexual union, as in 4:1.

records.source: וַיְהִ֖י בְּעֵ֣ת לִדְתָּ֑הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה תְאוֹמִ֖ים בְּבִטְנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And it was at the time of her giving birth, and behold, twins [were] in her womb.
pieces: When her time of delivery came, there were twins in her womb.

L.27: And it happened at the time she gave birth that, look, [there were] twins in her womb.

R.27: When Tamar was ready to give birth, she was carrying two babies, not one.

decisions.choice: twins in her womb: the words used of Rebekah
decisions.reason: The same words describe the birth of Esau and Jacob (25:24). Again the twins struggle over who comes first.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י בְלִדְתָּ֖הּ וַיִּתֶּן־יָ֑ד וַתִּקַּ֣ח הַמְיַלֶּ֗דֶת וַתִּקְשֹׁ֨ר עַל־יָד֤וֹ שָׁנִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֖ה יָצָ֥א רִאשֹׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was when she gave birth, and he put out a hand, and took the midwife and tied on his hand a scarlet [thread], saying, this one came out first.
pieces: During the birth one baby reached out a hand. The midwife caught hold of it and bound a scarlet thread on it, saying, "This is the first one out."

L.28: And it happened as she was giving birth that one put out a hand, and the midwife took [it] and tied a scarlet [thread] on his hand, saying, "This one came out first."

R.28: While she was in labor, one of the babies put out a hand. The midwife quickly tied a red thread around it. "He is the first one out," she said.

decisions.choice: tied a scarlet thread: marking the firstborn
decisions.reason: The firstborn received a double inheritance and leadership of the family, so the midwife marked which twin appeared first. Shani is a bright red dye or thread dyed with it.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀כְּמֵשִׁ֣יב יָד֗וֹ וְהִנֵּה֙ יָצָ֣א אָחִ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מַה־פָּרַ֖צְתָּ עָלֶ֣יךָ פָּ֑רֶץ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ פָּֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And it was, as he drew back his hand, and behold, came out his brother; and she said, what you have breached for yourself a breach! And called his name Perez.
pieces: Then the hand was drawn back, and his brother came out instead. "What a breakthrough you have forced for yourself!" said the midwife. And so he was named Perez.

L.29: And it happened, as he drew back his hand, that look, his brother came out. And she said, "What a breach you have made for yourself!" So his name was called Perez.

R.29: But the baby drew his hand back inside, and the other twin was born first. The midwife said, "You have pushed your way out!" So the boy was named Perez, which means "breaking out."

decisions.choice: Perez: "breach" or "breaking out"
decisions.reason: Perez (perets) sounds like the verb and noun in the midwife's words. The younger twin breaks through ahead of his brother. Perez becomes the ancestor of David (Ruth 4:18-22) and appears in the line of Jesus (Matthew 1:3).

decisions.choice: she said: most likely the midwife
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named; the midwife has just spoken in verse 28.

decisions.choice: the midwife
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the most likely speaker.

decisions.choice: which means "breaking out"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name.

records.source: וְאַחַר֙ יָצָ֣א אָחִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־יָד֖וֹ הַשָּׁנִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ זָֽרַח׃ס
records.gloss: And afterward came out his brother on whose hand [was] the scarlet [thread], and called his name Zerah.
pieces: Next his brother was born, the scarlet thread still on his hand, and he received the name Zerah.

L.30: And afterward his brother came out, who had the scarlet [thread] on his hand; and his name was called Zerah.

R.30: After him came the twin with the red thread on his hand. He was given the name Zerah.

decisions.choice: Zerah: "dawning" or "shining"
decisions.reason: The name comes from a verb used of the sun rising. It may recall the bright red thread, or the hand that appeared first like the first light.
